balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Enbridge Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Enbridge Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Enbridge Inc.: two EBITDA lines are shown. The GAAP-derived EBITDA column is built from the XBRL income statement and omits equity earnings from joint ventures (Gray Oak, DCP, etc.) and other income. Reported EBITDA is management's own non-GAAP figure, which includes those items and is the number guidance, segment EBITDA and the dividend-payout narrative are set against -- it is consistently the higher of the two.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)
  • The spread between the two EBITDA lines (equity earnings contribution)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Enbridge Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Enbridge Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Enbridge Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Enbridge Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Enbridge Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Enbridge Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

segmentEbitda.title: EBITDA by segment
segmentEbitda.content:
Enbridge reports EBITDA across four operating segments: Liquids Pipelines (crude oil/NGL transport, led by the Mainline system), Gas Transmission (long-haul natural gas pipelines, including the US Gulf Coast system), Gas Distribution & Storage (regulated utilities, mainly Enbridge Gas Ontario) and Renewable Power Generation (wind, solar and offshore assets).

For Enbridge Inc.: Liquids Pipelines is the largest and most stable segment and is the one most exposed to Mainline volumes; Gas Transmission is the fastest-growing on US data-centre and LNG-feedgas demand; Renewable Power is the smallest and most volatile, and has been shrinking as a share of the mix since the 2024 US gas-utility acquisitions shifted weight toward Gas Distribution & Storage.

What to watch:

  • Liquids Pipelines growth versus Mainline throughput (see Mainline Deliveries)
  • Gas Distribution & Storage's step-up from the 2024 utility acquisitions holding, not reversing
  • Renewable Power's shrinking share of total segment EBITDA

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Enbridge Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
